notes:
## Source content and physical page

The authorial foliation is **45** and the thin later foliation is **96**. No title or date is written. The page defines restriction of the indexed pro-neighborhoods to Z in (99), then gives a condition that Z be written **loc! fermée** and contain the stratum. An old difference expression and its NB are cancelled below a raised replacement parenthesis. The resulting map in (100) is described as a homotopy equivalence under the parenthetical assumption **X métrisable**. The author places a separate question above alors and the marginal **? à vérifier!** beside this statement. These are authorial reservations, not editorial additions.

The next paragraph generalizes the indexed neighborhoods to bands J and flags of bands. Formula (101) gives the tubular pro-neighborhood description, union over j in J, and the directed limit over Drap(J). The following NB says that the definition and two formulas **marche- / raient encore** for an arbitrary subset J of I. Formula (102) restricts V_J to Z; (103) and the diagram (104) give the annotated maps. The final condition is written Z⊃X_J with no star. In (104), the middle object is related vertically by two parallel strokes to V(X_J^*,Z). The lower comma and closing-parenthesis foot touch the scan’s lower cut, but both characters and the formula remain identifiable; no following text is supplied.

## Rereadings prompted by the notation and mathematical context

The index sequences were counted occurrence by occurrence. A point followed by a longer rule occurs in all three (99) indices, both (100) indices, the i-indexed V in the generalization paragraph, and between the two precedence signs of the written flag. The J-indexed V in that paragraph has point-rule-point. The first index in (99) additionally has explicit commas on both sides of its two continuation marks. None of these counts is regularized to a uniform ellipsis.

The final capital in the flag has bilateral bars and is read literally **I_n**, contrasted on the same line with J_0’s left-turning foot. The band-flag context would suggest J_n; that expectation prompted the local comparison but does not replace the visible I. Likewise, the first X superscript in (104) is h-shaped, with an upright and short right branches, unlike the radial stars in (103) and in the lower object of (104). The source therefore retains **h|*** with h first. The surrounding stratum notation suggests a star as a possible intended form, not a reason to erase the glyph uncertainty.

The raised parenthesis was inspected as a whole and in its crowded parts. **de sorte que** is clear. No independent star can be isolated on its first X, so the unstarred term stands first with the starred term retained as an alternative. The first connector is a plain shaft; its label remains uncertain where a descender from the previous line overlaps it. The second connector has a left hook/loop but no pointed right head. In (99), a blunt upturned endpoint leaves a narrow headless/headed alternative. The clear heads of (100), (103), both (104) arrows, and the directed-limit arrow provide local contrasts; their actual heads are retained. Where clear, h stands above the short parentheses enclosing a separate wave; the parentheses do not enclose h. The first crowded label remains uncertain.

Both subtraction signs in the cancelled line are short nearly horizontal bars. The dot above its first X_i_0 is visible in the whole formula even though it lies above the tighter beginning crop. The cancelled NB’s déf has a separate accent stroke. The first digits of (103) initially looked like a single bent shape; a tight crop shows a 1 joined to the flattened0, followed by3. The label is retained as103 from that geometry rather than from the numbering sequence.

## Words, punctuation and revisions

The two-line NB divides **marche-** and **raient**, with an independent line-end hyphen and a visible i dot in the second line. The blind audit supersedes the earlier ront hypothesis. C’s marchent doubt is resolved to this written split form without smoothing the tense or division. The following encore is legible. The caption writes **provoisinage** without a hyphen. The word est before un drapeau is live. Quotation marks are paired high ticks rather than guillemets.

The loc terminal is an uncrossed upright plus a detached dot, hence literal **loc!**, unlike a raised t. The marginal underline spans **à vérifier** and ends before the exclamation. The small independent question above alors is separated from the l ascender; no detached lower dot is exposed. The following low group remains on a/point-rule-point uncertain in the recorded audit. In (103), d’hom. has its final stop; in (104), d’hom has none. The parenthesis after métrisable has three distinct ellipsis points. The pale patch before métrisable is not transcribed; a separate dark accent-like mark over the e and the later i dot are visible.

All three C deletions and its raised insertion were reviewed for bounds and attachment. The first cancelled word remains fermé. The old lower word group permits only an unreadable left group and a tentative **du|de** on the right, where d is exposed but its ending is crossed. The long strike traverses the entire old mathematical line and leaves the raised replacement live. No comma follows that replacement’s closing parenthesis.

This reader performed transcription and local glyph comparisons, including the mathematical triggers described above, but no independent homotopy proof or other mathematical validation. No proof-check event is asserted; check_events remains empty.

The literal flag endpoint I_n is retained, as is the unstarred X_J at the end of104. The tiny first superscript in104 and the crowded raised first map label remain uncertain.
